alignments.note: Finite verb with its supplied subject pronoun under rule 9.
Dative pronoun rendered *thee*.
Improper preposition with the complex frame *in the sight of*, kept whole with its trailing *of* under rules 71 and 95 and headed on *sight*.
Article before θεοῦ; the ASV writes no determiner of its own for it, the frame's *the* belonging to ἐνώπιον (rules 23, 95).
Noun.
Substantival article before a participle with a single English word written for the pair; rule 90 gives it the relativizer *who*.

One Greek compound participle rendered *giveth life*; head on *giveth*, realizing the compound's verbal head -γονοῦντος, with *life* realizing ζῳο-. Heading on *life* by analogy to rule 91's `εὐχαριστέω` → *give thanks* remains defensible; the reading taken is that *give* here is not an empty support verb. ASV margin: *preserveth all things alive*.
Substantival adjective; the supplied *to* realizes the case and stays here under rule 21's determinerless clause, the ASV writing no *the* for the article to anchor.

Rule 102: the article governing a substantival adjective takes the supplied nominal *things*, headed on it. With no determiner written the article takes the nominal alone, the case preposition staying with the adjective under rule 21.
Conjunction.
Genitive continuing the ἐνώπιον frame; the case preposition *of* stays with the anarthrous name under rule 21's determinerless clause.
Name, split from Χριστοῦ under rules 17 and 26.
Substantival article before a participle with one English word written; rule 90 gives it *who*.
Preposition rendered *before*.
Name, split from Πιλάτου under rule 28.
Name.
Aorist participle rendered by the finite *witnessed*.
Article to *the*.
Attributive adjective.
Noun.

review_notes: τὰ πάντα is split with the supplied nominal *things* on the article (rule 102) and *to all* on the adjective; putting the whole *to all things* on πάντα under rule 17 is the competing reading, but rule 102 keeps a supplied nominal with the article that governs it.
Both τοῦ before participles take *who* under rule 90; τοῦ before θεοῦ is `unrepresented` because the frame's *the* belongs to ἐνώπιον.
